name: FPGA-NFC
one_line: FPGA ISO14443A reader built from discrete components rather than a dedicated RFID chip (Cyclone IV + 3Msps ADC), talking to MIFARE-class cards over serial.
why_notable: 146 stars, last commit 2024-01-26. Chip-free NFC reader implemented entirely in FPGA logic.

name: RFID HF Repeater Large
one_line: 13.56MHz field repeater placed between an obstruction and a reader to amplify coupling and gain a few extra millimeters of tag read distance.
why_notable: Same RFID field-manipulation category as the Extender Pro above, different form factor and use case.

name: Mellon
one_line: Python OSDP attack toolkit (passive eavesdropping, encryption downgrade, install-mode key extraction, weak-key brute force) run from a laptop through one to three USB-to-RS485 adapters.
why_notable: 114 stars, last commit 2023-08-15. Reference implementation behind Bishop Fox's OSDP 'Badge of Shame' research. Returned independently by two sub-searches.

name: RFIDetector
one_line: CERN-OHL-S credit-card-sized PCB that indicates whether a nearby RFID reader is emitting an LF (125kHz) or HF (13.56MHz) field.
why_notable: 3 stars, last commit 2024-03-22. No confirmed retail price - the figure is an unverified low-cost estimate.

name: simple_rfid
why_notable: 32 stars, last commit 2025-01-09. PCB files via PCBWay.

name: NFC Placard Mystery Pack
one_line: Pack of 3 random passive NFC tags (mix of NTAG213/NTAG215, some glow-in-the-dark) mounted on placards styled to blend into urban signage; writable for URL redirection or Amiibo-style emulation.
why_notable: Passive tags with no onboard logic of their own — closer to a consumable than a device; flagged borderline low-confidence since the DB scope explicitly covers RFID/NFC but also excludes generic items with no capability of their own.

name: HiLetgo PN532 NFC NXP RFID Module V3 Kit
one_line: PN532-chipset NFC/RFID reader-writer breakout board (I2C/SPI/HSU) that can read, write, and emulate 13.56MHz tags, used with libnfc/Arduino/Raspberry Pi.
why_notable: The PN532 chipset is the most widely used NFC controller in DIY/security tooling (libnfc-compatible, used in many RFID projects); this is a common low-cost breakout of it. Corroborated as a well-known module type via Adafruit's own PN532 breakout documentation, independent of this marketplace listing.

name: Proxmark3 Iceman Fork (RfidResearchGroup/proxmark3)
one_line: firmware only, needs Proxmark3 RDV4.01 or Proxmark3 Easy - replacement client/firmware adding extended LF/HF attacks, standalone modes and scripting over stock.
why_notable: De facto standard Proxmark3 firmware; 6045 stars, last commit 2026-09-10.

name: MACOBOX - Hardware Pentest Platform
one_line: All-in-one hardware pentesting platform for rapid connection, firmware dumping and analysis across multiple hardware interfaces.
why_notable: Top-end (~$11k) integrated hardware-hacking lab-in-a-box, the highest-priced item in the catalog and a distinct product tier from single-purpose tools like Bus Pirate or GreatFET.

name: ChipSHOVER
one_line: Motorized 3-axis XYZ positioning stage, 5 cm travel per axis, better than 200 nm precision and 4 um repeatability, for placing EM fault-injection probes or side-channel sensors over a die; driven from an LCD panel or Python.
why_notable: New product category for NewAE - a precision robotic positioner for chip-level probing.

name: CW310 Bergen Board (Large FPGA, K410T)
one_line: FPGA target board around a Xilinx Kintex K410T with a supervisory MCU for config/temp/voltage/clock control, DDR3+SRAM, JTAG/USB/PMOD headers, multi-stage VCC-INT filtering with inductive shunt and LNA for power analysis, and SMA/fan access for EM fault injection.
why_notable: Large-FPGA target for full SoC/crypto-core emulation in side-channel research. Out of stock (supply chain).

name: ChipWhisperer - HuskyPlus
one_line: Side-channel analysis and fault-injection platform, an upgraded model above the existing ChipWhisperer-Husky.
why_notable: Higher-end successor to the ChipWhisperer-Husky already tracked, now in scope under the professional-gear price allowance.

name: AutoProber
one_line: Automation stack combining a GRBL CNC (e.g. Genmitsu 3018), a USB microscope and a networked oscilloscope (Siglent SDS1104X-E) with a 3D-printed toolhead to map a PCB, identify pins and run operator-approved pogo-probe measurements with scope-based safety cutoffs.
why_notable: 330 stars, last commit 2026-04-16. Flying-probe automation normally only found in closed commercial lab gear; needs an assembled CNC+scope+microscope stack, not a single purchase.

name: PhyWhisperer-USB (CW610)
one_line: In-line USB 2.0 LS/FS/HS monitor and trigger box with a Spartan FPGA and 240 MHz clock; buffers 8,192 bytes, fires a cycle-accurate trigger on matched data patterns, has a power shunt and front-panel power-cycle button, and feeds sync clock/trigger to ChipWhisperer capture hardware.
why_notable: Returned by both the NewAE and Crowd Supply surveys at different prices - $360 direct, $365 on Crowd Supply. Times power-analysis and fault-injection captures against USB targets.

name: NewAE Probe Set with Power Supply
one_line: Isolated power module (5V USB in, +3.3V for LNA, +/-7.8V for the differential probe, up to 50V isolation) sold with a differential probe, an LNA probe and an H-field probe for measuring power and EM signals off a chip.
why_notable: Physical EM and power probes not covered by any tracked capture board; closer to sensing accessories than a standalone instrument.

name: CW308 UFO Board
one_line: Baseboard providing shared 1.2-3.5V supplies, an oscillator/crystal socket, on-board filtering for clean power measurement and diode-protected I/O for voltage glitching, accepting swappable 8-bit, 32-bit and FPGA target daughtercards.
why_notable: The standard target platform for ChipWhisperer side-channel and glitching work. Listed out of stock.
